summary:
Doppelgänger is an interactive web tool that scores how closely 30 Earth sites resemble the lunar south pole and Mars, on a 0–100 scale. The set includes 16 analog sites already used by NASA and ESA and 14 new candidates proposed by our team, 6 of them in Mexico. Each site is evaluated with 16 indicators grouped into 8 dimensions (geology, terrain, temperature, water, dust, life, subsurface and operations), using real data from NASA POWER and public NASA imagery. The Moon and Mars use different weights because each destination poses different constraints. Scores are classified as strong (70 or higher), partial (50–69) or weak (below 50).

To check the model, we tested it against known analogs: 9 of 12 lunar and 5 of 8 Martian analogs rank in the upper half of the list. Random changes of ±20% to the weights, repeated 300 times, keep the ranking nearly unchanged (mean Spearman ρ = 0.99).

The site also includes two simple simulators, solar energy generation and habitat heating, that compare each location with the Moon and Mars. It helps identify which Earth site best rehearses each challenge of a lunar or Martian mission, and shows where no Earth analog is enough.
